text.p: These are the main stories in Latvian newspapers on Monday. Prepared for Reuters by the Co-operation Fund. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:

- Leaders of the three major parties, Latvia's Way, Saimnieks and Fatherland & Freedom, held a meeting behind closed doors on Saturday to discuss a new government. Fatherland and Freedom has proposed Guntar Krasts, current economy minister. The position of Latvia's Way is not yet clear while Democratic Party Saimnieks has backed outgoing PM Andris Shkele.

- Krasts met president Guntis Ulmanis for consultations. Krasts agreed to undertake the forming of the government if asked to do so. The president said the final decision would be taken after the three major parties have agreed on a common candidate.
- Ulmanis held consultaions with five smaller parliament factions on the formation of a new government.
- Some 173 people have been frozen to death in Latvia last year.
- The 1997 state budget in January showed a surplus of 3.65 million lats. Overall state debt runs at 22.2 million lats.
- Controversial former finance minister Vassily Melnik said on Latvian TV on Sunday that his appointment to the post was opposed by people having squandered G-24 credits.
- President of the loss-making Latvian Shipping company - the world's 19th largest - was dismissed by the company's board on Friday. He will be replaced by the senior vice-president.

- The World Bank (WB) warned Latvia that relations are being strained after an appraisal of Laukkredits, the agency servicing a $25 million WB loan. The state audit says Laukkredits cannot service the credit because it is not a credit institution.

- The legal director of the Latvian Privatisation Agency Viktor Shadinov says the German concern Ruhrgas/Preussen Elektra, interested in privatising a minority share in Latvian Gas, is being scared away by Latvian Gas' enormous debts, amounting to 50.7 million lats.

- Total sales of Latvia's Balsam, the state-owned alcohol producer, amounted to 38.75 million lats. The company produces some 60 percent of alcohol made in Latvia, with 12 percent of it produce being exported.
